report: Patient is status post total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. A 4 cm complex cystic lesion is seen within the right ovary.
History of bilateral total knee arthroplasty. Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis and joint space narrowing are seen in the native right knee.
Status post right radical nephrectomy. Mild hydronephrosis is identified in the right kidney.
The patient has a known history of complete thyroidectomy. The thyroid gland is symmetrically enlarged and heterogenous.
History of left lower lobectomy. Expected postsurgical changes are present with volume loss and elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. The remaining left lung parenchyma is clear.
There is no pulmonary edema. Prominent bibasilar reticular opacities are stable and chronic, consistent with the patient's known idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Lungs are clear of acute consolidation. The previously seen right apical cavitary lesion has been surgically resected, with stable postoperative scarring and surgical clips now seen.
No acute intracranial hemorrhage or major vascular occlusion. Severe, confluent periventricular white matter hypoattenuation is noted, reflecting chronic small vessel ischemic disease.
No acute cardiopulmonary process. There is a new, large right-sided pneumothorax with mild leftward mediastinal shift compared to the prior radiograph.
The chest is radiographically stable. Interval development of moderate pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions is noted since the examination yesterday.
No acute findings are identified on today's study. There is a new, acute compression fracture of the L4 vertebral body with 50% height loss.
No acute cardiopulmonary process. Stable, chronic right-sided pleural thickening is noted, unchanged since the prior study from 2018.
No acute osseous abnormality. Old, well-healed wedge compression deformity of T12 is unchanged from multiple prior comparisons.
It cannot be definitively stated that there is no underlying mass, though none is visible on the current non-contrast study. Lungs are otherwise clear.
There is no radiologic evidence to exclude a tiny radiolucent foreign body, however, no opaque foreign body is definitively seen on this film.
I am entirely unable to see any evidence of an acute fracture on this study. A displaced, acute spiral fracture of the distal radius is clearly visualized.
We cannot rule out a subtle developing infiltrate in the clinical setting of fever; however, the lungs are completely opacified by massive bilateral effusions.
An azygos lobe variant is present in the right upper lung zone, created by the lateral downward invagination of the azygos vein. Lungs are clear.

A horseshoe kidney is noted, crossing the midline inferiorly to fuse at the lower poles. Both kidneys are entirely separate and located in their normal independent retroperitoneal anatomical positions.
Uterus didelphys is incidentally noted, demonstrating two distinct uterine horns and two cervices, consistent with the known Mullerian duct anomaly.
The patient has a known right-sided aortic arch. The descending thoracic aorta is seen normally traversing the left side of the spine.
The appendix is normal in caliber without evidence of acute appendicitis. A severely inflamed, dilated, and perforated appendix is surrounded by inflammatory stranding.
The endotracheal tube is in good position. The tip of the endotracheal tube is currently located in the right mainstem bronchus, resulting in complete collapse of the left lung.
